solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Student going further out grasped at rocks

indicators.note: to rock something is to shake it about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

explanation.surface: A climber reaching further out on a rock face clutches at the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all climbing, with 'going further out' and 'rocks' as a climber's words; in fact the definition ends at 'further', meaning further study after a first degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A postgraduate is a student who goes on to further study after a first degree.

clue.text: A third of prize fund Victor had not overlooked

parts.note: the first three of the nine letters of PRIZEFUND
Victor is V in the NATO alphabet
to have a meal is to eat it; had = ate

explanation.surface: Someone checks that Victor has not missed his third share of a prize fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' as in 'had dinner' gives ATE. 'Not overlooked' reads as 'not forgotten', but a private garden is one no neighbour can overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A private place is one that is not overlooked, out of sight of others.

clue.text: Second old drunk gulping sherry, half-cut — or worse

definitions.text: Second old drunk gulping sherry, half-cut — or worse

indicators.note: gulping means swallowing, so the jumbled letters take the shortened drink inside them
drunk means unsteady and reeling, so the letters of old are rearranged
half-cut means cut in half, so only the first half of sherry is kept

explanation.surface: An old drunk knocks back a second sherry and is getting tipsy, or worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue paints the answer: an old soak on his second sherry, tipsy or beyond. 'drunk' turns OLD into LOD, 'half-cut' trims SHERRY to SHE, and 'gulping' puts SHE inside LOD after S, giving LOSHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloshed is informal for very drunk, the state of someone tipsy or well beyond it.

clue.text: Scientific study hugely lacking content — below average effort, say, all round

indicators.note: below means, in a down clue, that the last piece is written under the rest
all round means turned right around, so these three pieces are read backwards

parts.note: par is the average or standard level, as in 'below par'
a go is an attempt or effort, as in 'have a go'
e.g. means 'for example', which is what say means here

indicators.note: lacking content means emptied of its middle, so only the first and last letters of hugely remain

parts.note: the word hugely with its inside letters removed keeps its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a scientific study that is hugely lacking in substance, a below-par effort all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' looks like part of 'below average' but places HY under the rest. 'all round' reverses PAR GO EG to give GEOGRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography is the scientific study of the Earth's surface, its features and peoples.

clue.text: First-class doctor introducing energy and new remedy

parts.note: A = first class, as in A1 or grade A
MD = Doctor of Medicine
E = energy, as in physics
n = new

explanation.surface: A top doctor brings in a new energy remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remedy' is a verb here, to put right, and AMEND matches it. The doctor and the remedy make the clue sound like medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend something is to remedy it: correct or put it right.

clue.text: City University starts to promote professors in review, unfortunately

indicators.note: take the starting letter of each of the next two words
to review is to look back

parts.note: U = university
the first letters of promote and professors
alas = unfortunately

explanation.surface: A city university's review has, unfortunately, turned down professors for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City University' reads as one name, the London university, but City is the definition and University just gives U. Uppsala is a Swedish city with a famous old university.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppsala is a city in Sweden, north of Stockholm.

clue.text: Weapon excessively constrains communist holding power

parts.note: too = excessively
a Red = a communist
P = power, as in physics

explanation.surface: A weapon is under strict control as a communist regime tightens its grip on power.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here, and 'constrains' fits the communist regime so well in the surface that it is easy to miss it as an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater weapon.

clue.text: Stomach ache convulsed bellboy with scowl

indicators.note: something convulsed is thrown into spasms, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters; 'with' just joins the two words

explanation.surface: A bellboy doubled up with stomach ache wears a scowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convulsed' fits the stomach ache so well that it hardly reads as an instruction. The collywobbles is a British informal word for a stomach upset, or for nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: The collywobbles is an informal name for stomach ache or an upset stomach, often from nerves.

clue.text: Gold coin supply initially offering liquidity within South American banks?

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: supply here is read as supple, flexibly, so the letters of coin are bent into a new order
initially means the first letter of offering is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word offering is the one taken

explanation.surface: A financial report about gold, coin and the liquidity of South American banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' sounds financial, as does 'liquidity', but the definition means water flowing between riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a great river of Venezuela and Colombia, a body of water held between South American banks.

clue.text: Leader not in mood for beheaded king

parts.note: TEMPER (mood) without its first letter
FOR without its first letter

explanation.surface: A leader who is not in the mood for a king who has lost his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like the definition and 'not in mood for' like a phrase; in fact 'Leader not in' strips TEMPER and the definition is 'king' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is a supreme monarch, a king of kings.

clue.text: It'll get you back on time — vessel, flash and extremely elegant

parts.note: re = on, concerning, as in a memo
t = time
an urn is a vessel
in a flash = in a tick, an instant

indicators.note: take the letters at the extremes, first and last, of 'elegant'

parts.note: the first and last letters of ELEGANT

explanation.surface: A smart, flashy boat that will bring you home on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back on time' reads as one phrase, but 'on time' gives RE and T. A return ticket covers the journey out and back, what Americans call a round-trip ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A return ticket pays for the journey home as well as the outward trip, so it gets you back.

clue.text: Left apple perhaps containing hard material

parts.note: L = left

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within

parts.note: an eater is an eating apple, as opposed to a cooker
H = hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An apple left out has a hard skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard material' looks like the definition, but 'hard' is only H. In Britain an eater is an apple for eating raw, as opposed to a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is a material made from tanned animal hide.

clue.text: Language is difficult to begin with — it takes up half a lecture

indicators.note: to begin with means the first letter of difficult is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word difficult is the one taken

indicators.note: takes up means absorbs or holds, so the two letters of it go around the shortened phrase
half means only the first half of the letters of a lecture are kept

explanation.surface: A language is hard at first, filling half a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' cuts A LECTURE to ALEC, and 'takes up' has IT hold that, giving IALECT after D.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional or social variety of a language.

clue.text: Handle strong joint when touring India

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all around it

parts.note: a weld is a joint made by fusing metal
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Handling a strong joint of cannabis while travelling around India.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests smoking in India, but the joint is a metal weld.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: wielding a sword or a tool means handling it with skill.

clue.text: Hairdo's damp swimming with duck in stream

indicators.note: the letters swim about into a new order

parts.note: to stream is to pour
anagram fodder with O
a duck is a score of nought in cricket: O

explanation.surface: A hairdo gets soaked while swimming with a duck in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The ducks and stream make a country scene, but 'stream' is the verb and the duck is a nought.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a hairstyle swept up high off the forehead.

clue.text: In some measure, uncovers upset and melancholy

parts.note: a mile is a measure of distance

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset turns the word upside down

parts.note: to bare is to uncover

explanation.surface: To some extent, someone uncovers things that are upsetting and sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In some measure' looks like the phrase 'to some extent', but 'In' is the container and 'some measure' is MILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable and melancholy both mean deeply unhappy.

clue.text: Be first to sympathise, bandaging servant's facial injuries

indicators.note: bandaging means wrapping around, so the outer letters enclose the word for servant
first to means the opening letter of sympathise is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word sympathise is the one taken
a lackey is a servant, especially a liveried footman

explanation.surface: Advice to be the first to show sympathy while bandaging a servant's injuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be first to sympathise' gives BE plus S, and 'bandaging' wraps BES round LACKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Black eyes are bruising around the eyes after a blow, injuries to the face.

clue.text: Plant-based food abandoned by popular French eatery

parts.note: an aubergine is a vegetable
in = popular, in fashion; removed

explanation.surface: Plant-based food falls out of fashion at a French restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant-based food' sounds like vegan fare, but it is simply a vegetable. An aubergine is what Americans call an eggplant.
explanation.definitionFit: An auberge is a French inn serving food.

clue.text: I throw cutting equipment in storage unit

parts.note: kit = equipment
used as printed
to lob is to throw

explanation.surface: Someone tosses cutting tools into a storage unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting equipment' looks like saws and knives; here 'cutting' is the container and a storage unit is a measure of data.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilobit, a thousand bits, is a unit of data storage.

clue.text: Footwear's unpleasant smell during day

parts.note: Sat = Saturday
BO = body odour

explanation.surface: Someone's shoes give off a bad smell during the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Smelly footwear is exactly the scene the surface paints, which is the joke. A sabot is the wooden clog that gave 'sabotage' its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, a piece of footwear.

clue.text: Relative's medical suspension to include iodine and boron

parts.note: a sling holds up an injured arm
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
B is the chemical symbol for boron

explanation.surface: A relative's liquid medicine is made up with iodine and boron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medical suspension' sounds like a liquid medicine, but it is a sling that suspends an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling, a brother or sister, is a close relative.

clue.text: Without Hollywood's backing, Brad Pitt plays minor role

indicators.note: plays means fools about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without means the letter that follows is taken out of Brad Pitt
backing here means the back or last letter of Hollywood is the one meant

parts.note: the name Hollywood, read without its possessive ending, supplies its back letter

explanation.surface: Without studio support, a film star ends up in a small part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' gives D, the last letter of Hollywood, which 'Without' removes from BRAD PITT before 'plays' rearranges the rest. 'backing' reads as financial support, but means the back letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit part is a small acting role with few lines, a minor role.

clue.text: Retired gangster secures daggers for border resident

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, as a pen secures sheep

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
an obelus is the dagger sign used in printing; plural obeli

explanation.surface: A retired gangster keeps knives to protect someone who lives by the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border resident' suggests someone living near a frontier; it is a plant in a garden border.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a small flowering plant often grown along the edge of garden borders.

clue.text: Tree in Hampshire town — photograph is taken

parts.note: Aldershot is an army town in Hampshire, an English county
a shot is a photograph; removed

explanation.surface: Someone photographs a tree in a Hampshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Photograph is taken' sounds like a snapshot of the tree; it tells you to take SHOT away.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family that grows near water.

clue.text: Billions invested in base in charge of autonomous machines

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it

parts.note: the root is the base of something
b = billion(s)
i/c = in charge

explanation.surface: Billions are being poured into a base run by machines that think for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invested' fits the money, but it only puts B inside ROOT. 'Of' belongs to the definition: robotic describes something of robots.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic means relating to robots, machines that act on their own.

clue.text: Scored Barcelona's opener — son was emotional about it

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: about it means going round the letter just named, so that letter sits inside the word for being emotional

parts.note: cried means was emotional, wept

indicators.note: opener means the first letter of Barcelona is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word Barcelona is the one taken

explanation.surface: A footballer's son weeps after Barcelona score the opening goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' reads as goals but means marked with lines. 'opener' gives B, and 'about it' has CRIED go round B, after S (son).
explanation.definitionFit: To scribe is to score or mark a line on wood or metal with a pointed tool.

clue.text: Capital Radio's focus is boring live band

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the letters go inside the word for live

parts.note: be means live or exist, as in 'to be or not to be'
Riga is the capital of Latvia

indicators.note: focus means the centre, so the middle letter of radio is taken

parts.note: the word radio, read without its possessive ending, has D as its middle letter

explanation.surface: A London radio station's main act is a dull live band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital Radio' looks like the London station, but Capital gives RIGA and 'focus' takes D, the middle of RADIO; 'is boring' puts RIGAD inside BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is an organised group of people, such as a fire brigade, so a band or company.

clue.text: Jabber sometimes confused things with crew

parts.note: a welter is a confused mass
w = with
an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: Someone babbles, sometimes mixing things up with the rest of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jabber' looks like a chatterer, but it is a boxer who jabs; 'sometimes' flags that a welterweight is only one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A welterweight is a boxer of a middle weight class, and boxers throw jabs.
